statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-128086 (GHSA-rrfc-gjm9-cgrj, GO-2026-6975): in go.opentelemetry.io/otel from 1.0.0-RC1 before 1.47.0, baggage.Parse and propagation.Baggage.Extract parse and copy every W3C baggage property up front, so a densely populated baggage header causes memory allocation out of proportion to its size. It is fixed in 1.47.0 by commit f09d1de, which parses properties lazily: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-rrfc-gjm9-cgrj, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/f09d1de32f4ac7e5ef16394533721106b1a57b89, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6975. We read every published build-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, from 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0, x86_64 and aarch64, after verifying each against its index checksum; 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves was the one read, and the other two listings, which cannot be downloaded, carry index build dates of 2026-06-17 and 2026-06-18, before go.opentelemetry.io/otel 1.47.0 was released on 2026-10-02, so none of the three can contain the fix. In every build the one ELF file in the package is the Go program /usr/bin/build. The function table (pclntab) of /usr/bin/build lists baggage.Parse, baggage.parseMember and propagation.Baggage.Extract (the functions GO-2026-6975 lists) in every build. Its build information records go.opentelemetry.io/otel 1.40.0 to 1.45.0 in every build up to 2.28.0-r4 and 1.47.0 from 2.28.0-r5 on, and only the 1.47.0 builds contain baggage.validateMetadata, baggage.normalizeMetadata and baggage.parsePropertyFields, which commit f09d1de adds. 2.28.0-r5 is the first fixed build.

Advisory: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-rrfc-gjm9-cgrj and fix commit: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/f09d1de32f4ac7e5ef16394533721106b1a57b89 which is in the v1.47.0 release tag and not in v1.46.0. Checked every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 33 builds, each for x86_64 and aarch64, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, each checked against the index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a statically linked Go program (no ELF interpreter). Its Go build information lists go.opentelemetry.io/otel v1.37.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r3; v1.39.0 in 0.20.0-r4; v1.42.0 in 0.21.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r9; v1.43.0 in 0.21.0-r10; v1.44.0 in 0.21.0-r11 to 0.21.0-r13; v1.45.0 in 0.22.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r4; v1.47.0 in 0.24.0-r5, but the vulnerable code is not compiled in. A byte search of every build for go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage., baggage.Parse, baggage.parseMember and propagation.Baggage.Extract also finds nothing. statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-128086 (GHSA-rrfc-gjm9-cgrj, GO-2026-6975): OpenTelemetry-Go's W3C baggage parser turns every property of a baggage member into a separate object while parsing, so a valid, densely populated baggage header causes memory allocation many times its own size, and a service that extracts baggage from untrusted requests can be made to do extra allocation and garbage collection. It affects go.opentelemetry.io/otel from 1.0.0-RC1 up to, but not including, 1.47.0, through go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage.Parse and its parseMember helper and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation.Baggage.Extract. 1.47.0 fixes it by storing property metadata compactly and building Property values only when they are asked for: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-rrfc-gjm9-cgrj, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/f09d1de32f4ac7e5ef16394533721106b1a57b89, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.47.0. Read the Go build information, the Go function table and the strings of /usr/bin/jaeger, the only file in the package and a statically linked Go program, in every published jaeger-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository: 21 builds from 2.19.0-r1 to 2.23.0-r4, for both x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against the index checksum and data hash. Builds 2.19.0-r1 to 2.22.0-r3 are built with go.opentelemetry.io/otel 1.44.0 (2.19.0-r1 to 2.20.0-r5) or 1.46.0 (2.21.0-r0 to 2.22.0-r3), and the function table of every one of them contains baggage.Parse, baggage.parseMember and propagation.Baggage.Extract, so they are affected. Builds 2.23.0-r0 to 2.23.0-r4 are built with go.opentelemetry.io/otel 1.47.0, and their function tables also contain validateMetadata, normalizeMetadata, parsePropertyFields and validPercentEncoding, baggage functions the fix adds, which no earlier build has (a byte search finds baggage.validateMetadata only in these builds). 2.23.0-r0 is the first fixed build. The jaeger-es-index-cleaner, jaeger-es-index-cleaner-dev, jaeger-es-rollover and jaeger-es-rollover-dev packages built from the same source, 2.20.0-r5 to 2.23.0-r4 for both architectures, link no go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage code and no propagation.Baggage method in any build.
